label: Physical prototypes
exact_claim: Italian prototype work characterizes residential and office buildings by use, construction period and envelope/HVAC properties rather than demographic user class.
scope: Published Italian zone-E prototypes; not the proposed simulation sample.
implementation_implication: Use the prototype library to document fixed physical inputs; do not label it a demographic archetype model.

label: Traceable reference-building libraries
exact_claim: The URBEM project formalizes harmonized Italian reference-building inputs in scorecards with source traceability and uncertainty labels.
scope: National Italian library workflow; library production, not an empirical energy prediction test.
implementation_implication: Adopt explicit provenance tables for every physical and user input.

label: Probabilistic parameter archetypes
exact_claim: Sokol et al. update distributions of uncertain residential archetype parameters using a training set and evaluate them on a separate larger set of homes.
scope: Cambridge MA low-rise homes; monthly/annual electricity and gas.
implementation_implication: Distinguish calibrated parameter distributions from demographic probabilities; copy no accuracy score.

label: Scale-specific physical representation
exact_claim: Ali et al. compare physical building archetypes developed at multiple Irish spatial scales and report differences when national archetypes are used locally.
implementation_implication: An Italian national user distribution does not by itself make a Padova dwelling sample representative.

label: Activity-driven appliance electricity
exact_claim: Richardson et al. combine active occupancy with daily activities to generate minute-resolution appliance electricity and compare simulated statistics with recorded dwelling electricity.
scope: 22 measured UKdwellings; electricity; one-year measurement stated in abstract.
implementation_implication: If archetype appliance electricity becomes internal gain, document thermal fractions and avoid treating all final electricity as zone heat.

label: Synthetic time-use activity sequences
exact_claim: Widén and Wäckelgård generate stochastic activities and household electricity from time-use-trained Markov processes.
scope: Swedish time-use basis; household electricity excluding heating/maintenance.
implementation_implication: Synthetic activity timing requires data beyond total heating hours; temporal resolution is not measurement resolution.

label: Occupancy-integrated physical archetypes
exact_claim: Buttitta et al. embed clustered time-use occupancy profiles within physical dwelling archetypes and explicitly map occupancy to assumed heating-control and internal-gain inputs.
scope: UKdwelling archetypes; EnergyPlus; annual heating contrasts.
implementation_implication: Occupancy-to-heating mapping is already an implemented approach; specify why the Italian demographic representation differs.

label: Stochastic occupancy categories
exact_claim: Buttitta and Finn provide stochastic multi-day occupancy-category profiles for occupancy-integrated archetype heating simulations.
implementation_implication: Presence categories are not identical to demographic household classes; do not rename one as the other.

label: Stochastic stock-scale occupant simulation
exact_claim: Chen et al. integrate stochastic occupant/end-use event schedules with ResStock and report checks against time-use data and measured end-use electricity.
implementation_implication: Do not claim first stochastic stock-scale household modelling, or characterize ResStock generically as fixed-schedule-only.

label: Population-based presence
exact_claim: Mosteiro-Romero et al. compare register-based individual daily schedules with standard-based deterministic and stochastic occupancy in district simulations.
scope: Mixed district uses including important educational context.
implementation_implication: This supports an assignment-method comparison, not transfer of its numerical differences to Italian homes.

label: Setpoint aggregation and thermal response
exact_claim: De Jaeger et al. compare alternative aggregation of occupant setpoint profiles because dwellings' thermal responses differ.
implementation_implication: Retain group-specific runs before aggregation; pooled mean inputs need a direct ablation rather than assumed equivalence.

label: Recent probabilistic occupancy application
exact_claim: Sood et al. train a probabilistic occupancy model from time-use data and apply it to Irish residential archetypes across spatial and temporal scales.
implementation_implication: No claimed small error percentages or universal geographic applicability until full evaluation design is inspected.

label: Thermostat-derived occupancy proxy
exact_claim: Jung et al.'s occupancy schedules describe inferred occupancy status rather than occupant count and their paper identifies sensor and ground-truth limitations.
implementation_implication: Measured thermostat records do not automatically give observed presence or household demographic membership.

label: Controller schedule versus runtime
exact_claim: Hanmer et al. distinguish programmed occupancy states and call-for-heat signals from actual presence and direct metered heating energy.
implementation_implication: Keep reported on-hours, encoded high-setpoint hours, positive-load hours and metered runtime distinct.

label: Stochasticity versus heterogeneity
exact_claim: Widén's aggregated occupancy-model comparison explicitly leaves inclusion of heterogeneity and end-use/building interactions as future work.
implementation_implication: Random schedules do not by themselves implement demographic diversity; archetype assignment and within-archetype variation are distinct factors.

label: Aggregation can reduce some behavioural variation
exact_claim: Gilani et al. find convergence of stochastic office-lighting predictions at larger simulated office aggregation scales.
implementation_implication: This is counterevidence to richer-is-always-needed; it does not establish convergence for residential heating or peaks.

label: Italian demographic user archetypes
exact_claim: Khajedehi et al. identify four Italian demographic user archetypes using household-age, household-size and education information.
implementation_implication: Implement the published or recovered fitted definitions; newly clustering is a different contribution requiring justification.

label: Probabilistic household–dwelling linkage
exact_claim: Khajedehi et al.'s dwelling-based linkage estimates probabilities of user types rather than a certain user class for a particular dwelling.
implementation_implication: Normalize/check probabilities, preserve support domain and uncertainty; do not select the most likely class without declaring the loss of diversity.

label: Italian outcomes have different evidence classes
exact_claim: Khajedehi et al. analyse declared daily heating on-hours and annual appliance electricity calculated from survey answers.
implementation_implication: These outcomes cannot validate modeled hourly demand or measured energy accuracy.

label: Simulation consequences remain a separate test
exact_claim: Khajedehi et al. explicitly name individual-building simulation impacts as future work.
implementation_implication: An implementation can assess consequences, while the paper's forward-looking accuracy rhetoric supplies no validation result.

label: Prior ISTAT schedule construction
exact_claim: Prataviera et al. already construct random profiles from three ISTAT heating-use time bands and perturb operating duration/start-up time in EUReCA uncertainty analysis.
implementation_implication: Neither three-band reconstruction nor randomness is new; isolate the added archetype dimension explicitly.

label: Measured versus unmeasured applications
exact_claim: Prataviera et al.'s Verona evaluation uses selected measured district-heating periods, whereas their larger Milan application lacks those measurements.
implementation_implication: Use site-specific validation labels and align usefulheat/meterboundaries; no inherited Padova accuracy.

label: Aggregation and schedule representation
exact_claim: Ferrando et al. compare smart-meter-informed randomized occupant-related schedules with a baseline at multiple temporal and spatial aggregation levels.
implementation_implication: Schedule-detail effects depend on endpoint/scale; do not equate one household result with national totals.

label: Italian survey stock-model precedents
exact_claim: MOIRAE and MODENA already use Italian household-survey information for bottom-up energy modelling.
implementation_implication: Survey use itself is established; separate code lineage from thematic similarity.

label: Italian stock scenarios already exist
exact_claim: MODENA work already considers weather, envelope renovation and heating-technology scenario changes.
implementation_implication: Multi-weather or retrofit scenarios alone do not establish novelty; design matched user-representation factors.

label: Building-type survey profiling precedent
exact_claim: Puglisi et al. classify Italian survey dwellings into building-type classes to construct energy profiles.
implementation_implication: Building-typology segmentation differs from demographic user identification; distinguish both from the CLIMA full-stock model.

label: Synthetic linkage is not observed pairing
exact_claim: Latifi et al. probabilistically link population, building, activity and weather sources and acknowledge missing individual linkage ground truth.
implementation_implication: Probabilistic synthetic assignment needs internal checks, uncertainty propagation and separate external evaluation.

label: Nonresidential stochastic schedules are an adjacent comparator
exact_claim: Dabirian et al. compare deterministic and measured-data-derived stochastic schedules in five Montreal institutional office buildings.
implementation_implication: An office accuracy improvement cannot be imported into Italian demographic archetype heating.

label: Heating timing dispersion has prior RC evidence
exact_claim: Koene and Eslami-Mossallam examine temporal thermostat-setting dispersion with an RC district heating model.
implementation_implication: Settings estimated from energy and then compared with that evidence do not automatically establish independent holdout validation.

label: Observed heating-pattern heterogeneity
exact_claim: Huebner et al. infer diverse English heating patterns from indoor-temperature series and compare them with common modelling schedules.
implementation_implication: Temperature-inferred operation differs from direct controller/metered data; observation geography is not Italian.

label: Controlled profile/climate sensitivity precedent
exact_claim: Rugani et al. compare occupancy-profile databases in EnergyPlus under three city climates for a standard building and multiple uses.
implementation_implication: Database choice changes multiple input assumptions; no imported extreme percentage differences or empirical accuracy inference.

label: CLIMA foundation and related archetype contribution are distinct
exact_claim: The CLIMA chapter presents regional-resolution survey-informed stock energy modelling, while the separate 2025 archetype paper identifies demographic groups, dwelling linkage and survey-derived patterns.
implementation_implication: Use conferenceclaims only from its completepageaudit; archetypeimplementation should extend the foundation without re-claiming groupdiscovery.

label: Broader literature does not establish the proposed result
exact_claim: Existing archetype/schedule studies justify testing explicit representation choices but do not establish that the planned Italian implementation improves measured accuracy.
scope: Comparative interpretation of bounded primary findings; no new calculatedquantity.
implementation_implication: Register improvement as a hypothesis requiring independent matched evaluation; publish sensitivity/nullfinding if that is what runs establish.
